title: Edoardo Makes Space for Ambitious Goals, Anchored in Family and Passion
summary: Edoardo, a 15-year-old swimmer from Italy living with achondroplasia and albinism, is dreaming big – from Paralympic competition to Formula 1 engineering.
body_markdown:
At 15, Edoardo is training for a future that could take him from the swimming pool to the Paralympics – and one day, into the world of Formula


1


engineering.


It’s an ambitious path for a high school student at the International School of Como in Italy, but Edoardo’s goals are rooted in the same qualities that define his everyday life: curiosity, discipline and a steady belief that possibility is an open swim lane. He speaks three languages, balances school with competitive swimming, music and motorsports and is already building the life he dreams about.


“I’m making space for my future,” says Edoardo. “I’m training with hopes of competing in the Paralympics; whether in Los Angeles in 2028 or Brisbane in 2032. But I also dream of someday working in motorsport, maybe even with a Formula 1 team.”


BioMarin’s Making Space series spotlights people like Edoardo – individuals, caregivers and advocates of individuals


living with skeletal conditions whose daily lives reflect drive and determination.


Edoardo trains almost every day, finding balance between school, sports and creativity. Beyond swimming, he spends his free time DJing, cycling and practicing on his racing simulator, always looking for something new to learn. He listens to everything from piano music to emerging Italian rap artists.


Swimming has become both a discipline and a source of freedom for him.


“In the water, he feels strong and independent,” says his mother, Isabella. “He’s free from assumptions and full of focus. When he swims, listens to music or talks about cars, his joy fills our home.”
